messagingGuides.documentName: OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift Messaging Guide.html
messagingGuides.summary: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift allows organizations to migrate virtual machines (VMs) to a fully managed, modern infrastructure, providing a flexible and consistent platform for both VMs and containers. This solution aims to simplify operations, reduce costs, and accelerate modernization efforts by leveraging the combined expertise of Red Hat and Microsoft.
keyPoints: OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift enables organizations to migrate their virtual machines (VMs) from existing virtualization platforms to a fully managed, modern infrastructure.
This solution provides a flexible and consistent middle ground where VMs can benefit from OpenShift's cloud-native management capabilities without deploying additional hardware.

Azure Red Hat OpenShift offers a unified, hybrid-cloud, open source infrastructure management stack that supports VMs and containers side by side, reducing the complexity of the cloud-native transition.
OpenShift minimizes operational overhead with a consistent platform across on-premise, public cloud, and edge environments, managed through a single interface.
Built-in tools like the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization and Ansible Automation Platform simplify the migration process from legacy platforms with minimal disruption.
Deploying VMs on Azure Red Hat OpenShift reduces operational complexity, risk, and costs through a managed, first-party Azure solution.
The platform offers automated Day 2 operations, integrated tools, and processes from both Red Hat and Microsoft, leading to efficiencies and potential reductions in VM and cloud compute spend.
OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift provides a secure, enterprise-grade platform, integrating security tools, continuous vulnerability monitoring, and compliance standards.
The platform supports innovation and modernization by allowing integration of containers and AI workloads within a unified hybrid cloud environment.
Organizations can optimize cloud costs by right-sizing VMs, utilizing smaller instance types, and benefiting from Azure's operational expenditure model.
The Azure Hybrid Benefit allows reuse of existing on-premises licenses for RHEL and Windows Server, maximizing license value and further reducing costs.
Customers can apply their Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC) toward Azure Red Hat OpenShift and benefit from a single bill.
Azure NetApp Files (ANF) can be used as a high-performance, enterprise-grade file storage option for mission-critical workloads on OpenShift Virtualization on ARO.
talkTracks: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift is uniquely positioned to help customers accelerate the migration of their traditional VMs to a scalable, cloud-native application platform.
This infrastructure empowers organizations with a flexible, consistent platform for deploying both VMs and containers across hybrid environments.
Through the Migration Toolkit for Virtualization and Ansible Automation Platform, customers can easily transition from legacy platforms with minimal disruption.

Deploying VMs on Azure Red Hat OpenShift reduces operational complexity, risk and costs with a managed, first-party Azure solution built on Red Hat's open-source innovation and RHEL experience, and Microsoft's cloud expertise.
Automated Day 2 operations, integrated tools and processes across both Red Hat and Microsoft, and reductions to VM and cloud compute spend further drive efficiencies.
OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift delivers a secure, enterprise-grade platform with integrated security tools, continuous vulnerability monitoring, and compliance standards.
Azure Red Hat OpenShift provides a future-ready platform that supports innovation and modernization efforts for VM-based applications using a cloud-native approach to development and delivery.

Organizations can seamlessly transition from traditional virtualization platforms with Red Hat and Azure support, leveraging established migration frameworks that minimize downtime and operational risks.

OpenShift Virtualization provides a unified view and consistent operational model for managing application workloads across on-premises, Microsoft Azure, and edge environments, enhancing efficiency and collaboration.
Integration with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform and Advanced Cluster Management for Virtualization (ACM-V) provides a robust solution for automating and managing VMs and their infrastructure.
Customers benefit from a fully managed platform through Azure Red Hat OpenShift, backed by a specialized 24x7 global SRE team, preserving familiar workflows while enabling modernization.
OpenShift Virtualization allows organizations to expand their virtualization strategy by integrating containers, cloud-native applications, and AI workloads within a unified hybrid cloud environment.

Organizations can unlock greater business value by reducing the need for ongoing platform and resource management, allowing IT teams to focus on strategic innovation and emerging technologies like generative AI.
OpenShift Virtualization on Azure Red Hat OpenShift enables organizations to optimize cloud costs by right-sizing virtual machines and utilizing smaller instance types and fewer vCPUs.
Customers benefit from the cloud's operational expenditure model and can further reduce costs with the Azure Hybrid Benefit by reusing existing on-premises licenses for RHEL and Windows Server.

As an Azure first-party service, Azure Red Hat OpenShift is natively integrated within the Azure portal, providing seamless access to Azure services like Entra ID, Azure Monitor, and Azure OpenAI for enhanced security and operations.
Azure Red Hat OpenShift meets rigorous compliance standards and offers trusted, cloud-native security solutions to protect workloads across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

battlecards.summary: Red Hat OpenShift offers customers the flexibility to re-use existing certified hardware and provides a comprehensive hybrid multicloud environment with integrated virtualization and containerization capabilities, while Azure Local (Azure Stack HCI) forces hardware refresh and is a Microsoft lock-in platform. OpenShift also serves as a stepping stone to application modernization and AI/ML capabilities.
keyPoints: Red Hat OpenShift allows customers to re-use existing certified hardware, whereas Azure Local requires new prescribed certified hardware.
OpenShift provides a single platform for virtualization and containers (Kubevirt), with ACM and Ansible for management, supporting disconnected environments.
Azure Local utilizes prescribed Azure services and the Azure Console, with containers running on an AKS distro of Kubernetes and VMs migrated to Hyper-V, and does not support disconnected operations.
Red Hat OpenShift includes RHEL for Linux guests, while Azure Local supports Azure Linux, RHEL, SUSE, and Ubuntu for Linux guests.
Neither Red Hat OpenShift nor Azure Local include Windows guest support.
OpenShift uses MTV for migration, while Azure Local uses VMM and Starwind.
OpenShift is available in appliance form factors from DELL APEX, IBM Fusion, and HPE Greenlake.
Azure Local (Nutanix-based HCI) offers limited modernization to containers, with virtual machines as the primary workload, and is Microsoft-centric.
OpenShift provides an opportunity to modernize to containers, with virtual machines as first-class citizens, and includes an AI platform (SKU add-on).
Azure Local leads to Microsoft lock-in, while OpenShift offers a modern application platform with VMs supporting hybrid multicloud environments.

Operational and cost efficiencies.
Increased scalability and cloud elasticity.
keyPoints: Siemens selected Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization as the strategic alternative to VMware post-Broadcom acquisition.
Red Hat Services provided comprehensive support including discovery workshops, training, and TAMs for successful migration and adoption.
The solution was tailored to three distinct customer groups: small/medium VM operators, critical factory workload owners, and large-scale datacenter operators.
Siemens aims to achieve technical, cost, and operational benefits through platform standardization and modernization.
The project emphasizes training and community building for long-term success and knowledge sharing.

caseStudies.challenge: ICON faced the challenge of rapidly accelerating its AI adoption, reducing cloud spend, and speeding up time to market to remain competitive. They also needed an alternative to expensive and unscalable existing platforms (like Mirantis Kubernetes Engine and VMware) that could provide cloud-like capabilities within their own data centers.
caseStudies.solution: ICON partnered with Red Hat to implement Red Hat OpenShift AI and Red Hat OpenShift Platform Plus to manage AI and machine learning models across hybrid cloud environments. They also utilized Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to automate infrastructure provisioning and are considering replacing VMware with Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization.
results: Reduced timeframe for provisioning infrastructure and virtual machines for developers from 3 weeks to 30 minutes.
Enabled faster launch of new apps and features with a better user experience.
Improved application performance and stability.
Potential to avoid rising costs associated with Broadcom/VMware.
Established a consistent platform for running containerized workloads and virtualized machines.
keyPoints: ICON is a well-known brand and a potential reference for other customers.
Red Hat is seen as a strategic partner due to a long-standing relationship and successful past projects.
The sales cycle for this project was unusually short (3.5 months) due to the trusted partnership.
This win demonstrates Red Hat's expertise in virtualization and AI in a heavily regulated industry.
The project created a repeatable framework for similar deployments.

AI/ML platform: cloud, datacenter, Edge.
Appliance solution from DELL, HP, IBM.

talkTracks: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization offers a path to modernization for VMware workloads, enabling customers to containerize applications and integrate AI platforms, unlike AWS EVS which primarily provides VMware on AWS without modernization.
Highlight Red Hat's open-source nature and robust partner ecosystem as a differentiator from AWS EVS, which is a beta offering with potential price risks from VMware.

Emphasize Red Hat OpenShift's flexibility in hardware choice and its ability to re-use existing hardware, contrasting with AWS Outposts' requirement for AWS-provided hardware, which can lead to vendor lock-in.
Discuss the unified management benefits of OpenShift Virtualization for both containerized and VM applications, a feature not present in AWS Outposts or Azure Stack solutions.

Position OpenShift as a complete cloud-native application platform that offers an open solution with no lock-in, including RHEL and extensive enterprise experience, in contrast to the more constrained AWS offerings.
keyPoints: AWS Elastic VMware Service (EVS) allows customers to run VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) within Amazon VPC, enabling migration of VMware-based VMs to AWS using existing VCF software and tools without refactoring.
Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization provides an application platform with full virtualization, supporting modernization to containers, and offers VMs as first-class citizens, including an AI platform.
AWS Outposts is an on-premise offering of selected AWS services, leading to AWS lock-in.
Red Hat OpenShift is an open solution with no lock-in to any cloud provider or hardware, featuring 100% open source, RHEL inclusion, and 25 years of enterprise experience.
A key distinction is hardware flexibility: Red Hat OpenShift allows re-use of existing certified hardware, while AWS Outposts requires AWS-provided hardware.

keyDifferentiators: Complete virtualization and backup solution with Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization and Commvault Cloud integration.
Robust offering that includes backup and cybersecurity capabilities baked in.
Unified management platform, ingrained data security, and scalable performance.
Ability to recover from major outages or ransomware attacks.

Commvault alone may not offer complete recovery capability for critical OpenShift environments in case of disaster or cyberattack.

Emphasize the potential for "Bigger Deals" as customers perceive a more complete offering.
Stress the "Accelerated delivery time" because customers avoid comparing and evaluating third-party backup solutions.
Address objections about existing backup solutions by questioning their seamless integration with OpenShift and their ability to handle complex recovery mechanisms.
Counter objections about the cost of the integrated solution by highlighting the even greater cost of recovering from a major outage or ransomware attack without comprehensive protection.
keyPoints: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization Migration and Commvault Cloud provide a combined solution for backup, recovery, and data protection.
The integrated solution offers a unified management platform, security, and scalable performance while reducing costs.
Key benefits include granular recovery, data lifecycle management with compliance features, and automated disaster recovery.
The solution addresses customer pain points related to complexity, security, compliance, and reliable disaster recovery.
Red Hat and Commvault are industry leaders, offering a stronger combined solution.

competitiveReviews.documentName: Google Cloud Platform or OpenShift_ Virt
competitiveReviews.competitor: Google Cloud Platform (Google Distributed Cloud, Google GKE Enterprise VM Runtime, Google Cloud VMware Engine)
keyDifferentiators: OpenShift with Virtualization offers choice of certified hardware, allowing customers to reuse existing hardware.
OpenShift Virtualization is Operator-based and supports live migration of VMs.
Red Hat includes RHEL as a Linux guest (though not with OVE) and offers MTV for migration.
OpenShift supports OpenShift Data Foundation, CSI, and other storage solutions.
OpenShift provides extensive observability through OpenShift Observability.
competitorWeaknesses: Google Distributed Cloud relies on partner hardware and provides GKE Enterprise/GKE Enterprise for software, which is less flexible.
Google GKE Enterprise VM Runtime is not Operator-based and does not support live migration.
Google's VM runtime (Kubevirt) extends Kubevirt with Google proprietary virtual switch technology.
Google Cloud VMware Engine provides simple migration of VMware without modernization to containers.
Google Cloud VMware Engine does not support managing VMs using Pipelines in a cloud-native way, relying on traditional VMware on Google Cloud.
talkTracks: Highlight OpenShift's integrated approach to containers and VMs as a key differentiator for modernization.
Emphasize the benefits of OpenShift's Operator-based virtualization and live migration capabilities.
Discuss OpenShift's flexibility in hardware choices and reuse of existing infrastructure.
Position OpenShift as a strategic platform for customers looking to evolve their infrastructure beyond traditional VMware.
Showcase OpenShift's comprehensive observability and cloud-native management features for VMs.
keyPoints: Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization offers a more integrated and cloud-native approach to managing VMs and containers compared to Google's offerings.
OpenShift provides greater flexibility in hardware and supports live migration, which Google's GKE Enterprise VM Runtime lacks.
Google Cloud VMware Engine focuses on migrating existing VMware environments but does not offer the same level of modernization or cloud-native VM management as OpenShift.
Red Hat OpenShift is positioned as an application platform that includes virtualization as a first-class citizen, enabling a path to containerization and AI/ML.
OpenShift's robust storage, observability, and management features for VMs provide a comprehensive solution.

competitorWeaknesses: VMware Fault Tolerance and Site Recovery Manager are expensive and intricate to configure.
VMware Fault Tolerance requires the VM to run twice, imposing significant latency and throughput requirements, which Red Hat does not have a direct equivalent to.
talkTracks: Do not try to rip and replace VMware HA/DR functionality; avoid feature comparisons.
Have a conversation with your customer and understand their AH & DR requirements.
Discuss if the customer truly uses VMware Fault Tolerance and Site Recovery Manager in their production environment, given their expense and complexity.

When a customer asks about DRS, SRM, or fault tolerance, determine if they are asking about dynamic workload distribution, automated recovery/redeployment, or continuous availability with millisecond-level downtime, respectively, and respond accordingly.
keyPoints: OpenShift Virtualization offers High Availability and Disaster Recovery solutions.
High availability ensures an application is available even during infrastructure failure, by restarting VMs on another host, with some delay.
Disaster recovery involves recovering from major disasters like earthquakes or floods.
Site recovery is a business continuity and disaster recovery solution for VM recovery between sites.
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the targeted time to restore a business process after disruption.

Showcase OpenShift's integrated approach to VMs, containers, and serverless as a modern cloud-native solution.
Address concerns about the long-term support and future of oVirt, given Oracle's minimal contributions and Red Hat's cessation of support.

OpenShift Virtualization offers an integrated, comprehensive platform for both VMs and containers, supporting cloud-native development.
The future of oVirt, on which Oracle Virtualization is based, is uncertain due to minimal contributions from Oracle and a lack of community health.
Red Hat is a major contributor to CNCF projects and a leader in container management and DevOps platforms.
OpenShift provides extensive partner support and a robust roadmap, ensuring long-term viability and innovation.

keyDifferentiators: Backed by IBM.
Strong contributions to open source, demonstrating leadership and support.
Large partner ecosystem for certified hardware and software, facilitating migrations from VMware and AI solutions.
Published roadmap offering clear vision for customers.
Robust security and industry certifications.
competitorWeaknesses: VMware vCloud Foundation (VCF) 5.2 EOL in Oct 2027.
VCF requires license usage submission every 180 days, or hosts disconnect from vCenter and new workloads cannot be started if entitlement is exceeded.
VMware are not in the top 20 contributing organizations for integrated Argo CD, native CI/CD, and Istio.
VMware's partner ecosystem is contracting to a smaller, more focused, invite-only model, creating uncertainty for customers.
VMware's vSphere Foundation update in 11/2024 shows a price increase from $135/core and a 2.5x increase in vSAN capacity.
talkTracks: Highlight Red Hat's strong commitment to open source and its comprehensive, enterprise-ready solutions, emphasizing the 'managed risk' approach.
Discuss the strategic advantage of OpenShift Virtualization as a Kubernetes-native platform for unifying application and VM management, contrasting it with VMware's traditional virtualization.
Emphasize Red Hat's extensive partner ecosystem and transparent growth as indicators of stability and future-proofing.
Address VMware's licensing complexities and ecosystem contraction, positioning Red Hat as a more flexible and future-proof choice.
Explain how OpenShift Virtualization empowers organizations to modernize their IT infrastructure at their own pace, offering a clear path to cloud-native adoption without a rip-and-replace strategy.
keyPoints: Red Hat is positioned as an open-source, Kubernetes-native, and cloud-native alternative to VMware's traditional virtualization and proprietary solutions.
OpenShift Virtualization offers a unified operational model for both modern containerized applications and traditional VMs, leveraging Kubernetes as the control plane.

VMware vCloud Foundation (VCF) is an evolved SDDC modernization focused on maintaining traditional vSphere administrative structures, with potential licensing complexities and a contracting partner ecosystem.
Red Hat's approach reduces vendor lock-in, provides greater flexibility, and supports a direct path to cloud-native adoption and application modernization.
KubeVirt, an open-source project, enables VMs to be treated as first-class citizens within a Kubernetes environment, offering community-driven innovation and broad industry adoption.
